chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Kahmas (and his name is Haytham ibn Ubayd), from a man from the people of Wasit, from our companions, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My uncle divorced his wife three times, one divorce in each purity period.' He said: 'Tell him to have her reviewed (by a new marriage contract), because the meaning in this report is that we assume he issued one additional divorce without a review, for we only permit the three divorions for the sake of the Sunnah in one purity period if he reviews between each two divorces, even if that is in one purity period, as we have clarified.'
ai.seo_question: How does the Shia school validate three divorces issued in separate purity periods?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that divorcing three times within a single purity period requires a 'review' (raj'a) between each instance to align with the Sunnah of one divorce per period. This ruling ensures the three divorces are treated as a valid sequence rather than three separate, immediate divorces, thereby preserving the wife's right to a proper waiting period (iddah) before the finality of the divorce. This interpretation reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on procedural correctness in marital dissolution to prevent hasty or invalid divorces.
